NEVORA · Direction B · Nov 10, 2026

NEVORA UI Review

A full review of every screen for Owner, Manager, Employee and Lead at 320, 390, 768, 900, 1280 and 1440 pixels wide, plus the Clocker kiosk, the sign-in and public pages, and the phone-app screens. Eleven passes looked at layout, colour, type, buttons, icons, menus, states, accessibility, wording in English and Spanish, and the design-system code. Findings that several passes reported are merged into one, keeping the highest severity and every original ID.

Fix first

The 15 findings that most affect trust, payroll and everyday use. Each links to its full card below.

  1. 1HighNV-001

    Going offline wipes the loaded page while the banner says "Showing what was loaded"

    When the connection drops after a page has loaded, Home, Timecards, Things to do, Time and Pay replace their content with "View paused" or an empty card. The shell banner says "You're offline. Showing what was loaded." at the same moment, and each page words the paused state differently.

    Fix. Pick one rule (see Decisions). Either keep body.content rendered read-only while phase is 'paused', with an amber "Offline · updated 9:24 PM" line and actions disabled, or keep the clearing and change the banner to "You're offline. Reconnect to see the latest." Use one paused message on every page.

  2. 2HighNV-002

    "Done and older" hides pending approvals

    The page called "Done and older · Not counted in today's total" holds 18 timecards to approve, two time corrections waiting for review, 47 plan-ahead items and coverage gaps. An Owner or Manager who clears Things to do to zero still has 70+ open items.

    Fix. Move Time corrections and Timecards to approve into Things to do as their own groups. Rename the entry "Later and done" with a count ("Waiting 22 · Done 4") and keep only decided items under Done.

  3. 3HighNV-006

    The timecard backlog shows a different count on every screen

    The same pending timecards read 11 on Home, "Approve 7 timecards first" on Time exports, "12 not finalized" in export options, 18 under Done and older and "Approved 0/12" on Timecards. One Timecards screen shows "Ready to approve 6" beside "Approve 3 ready", and "Attention 4" can't be traced to rows.

    Fix. Use one shared selector for "timecards to approve before payroll" on Home, Payroll, Time exports and Things to do, and name the scope on every count ("11 timecards from Nov 2–8"). Make the Attention tile filter the list and give each affected row an amber chip.

  4. 4HighNV-007

    The Payday card hides overdue payroll and says "Ready now" for unreviewed work

    Home shows next Friday's payday with an amber "In 11 days" chip while Payroll says two pay periods have no payroll and the Nov 6 payday has passed. Its three progress segments are unlabelled and never light, yet the line reads "11 timecards to review · Ready now".

    Fix. When overdue periods exist, show the oldest with a red "Payday passed Nov 6" chip and "Prepare Oct 26 – Nov 1". Label the segments (Timecards, Review pay, Approve) or drop them, and replace "Ready now" with the state ("0 of 11 approved"). Hide the segments for roles without payroll.

  5. 5HighNV-024

    Payday countdown and dates disagree because Payroll uses the UTC date

    One payday (Fri, Nov 20) is 11 days away on Home and My pay but 10 days away on Payroll. It is also styled three ways: amber chip, green chip and grey text. Payroll settings shows a change dated tomorrow.

    Fix. Derive today in the company time zone, as Home does. Format "Change history" in that zone too. Use one payday chip everywhere: amber while timecards wait and green when ready (home-b.tsx:144–146 already has this logic). Reuse it in payroll-runs.tsx:214 and My pay.

  6. 6HighNV-039

    Home tells someone who is already clocked in to clock in

    Time says "Right now · On the clock · Clocked in at 12:02 PM · 9 h 24 min so far". Home's "On shift now" card says "Clock in on the Main Office tablet · Breaks and clock out happen there too". The instruction never changes with the clock state, so Home contradicts Time and can send someone back to the tablet to punch twice.

    Fix. In src/components/employee-b/home-b.tsx:122-123, branch the tinted notice on the punch state. The hero already reads Time's records (hoursAuthority), so the state is available. When clocked in: a green dot with "Clocked in at 12:02 PM" and "Breaks and clock out on the Main Office tablet". When the shift has started and there is no punch: an amber "Not clocked in yet" with "Clock in on the Main Office tablet".

  7. 7HighNV-003

    White text and glass chips on the teal band fail contrast

    Band sub-lines, live-figure labels, week-day letters, segment labels and search placeholders use 17 different white alphas and read at 3–4:1. Glass status chips ("Live", "Due", "Now", "Shift lead", "Tomorrow") measure 3.6–4.4:1, and the Clocker's "TIME CLOCK" label is 3.72:1.

    Fix. Add two tokens: --b-on-band #FFFFFF for titles, figures and labels on glass, and --b-on-band-2 rgb(255 255 255 / .86) for sub-lines on solid band only. Delete the other 15 alphas. On the hero, use solid white chips with status ink (#8A4B00 amber, #1D6B45 green, #0B6E69 teal).

  8. 8HighNV-004

    Phone tab-bar labels fail contrast on every page

    The bottom tab labels are 10.5px grey #7D868B on a white bar, 3.71:1 (axe flags 3.68:1 on every phone capture). They are the primary navigation on every phone page for all four roles.

    Fix. Set inactive labels to #6A7176 (4.96:1 on white) and keep the teal active state. Size stays 10.5px as approved.

  9. 9HighNV-008

    Tap targets fall under the 48px rule on phones and tablets

    Phone week arrows are 32–36px, sheet Save and Edit pills 36px, segments 34–36px, switches 51×31 and person checkboxes 20px. On touch tablets the rail is 40×48, top-bar controls 40px, back links 32px and schedule grid blocks 28px, because the desktop layer starts at 768px with no touch pass.

    Fix. Extend the kit's ::after hit area (owner-b.css:84) to .b-week__arrow, .q-nav__r, .c-shift__save, .b-seg > *, .b-btn--glass and row buttons. Inside the tablet block add @media (pointer: coarse) with a 44px floor and 48×48 rail links. Make switch and checkbox rows the <label>. Use one row-action size (44px hit, 96px min width) and one footer-action size (48px).

  10. 10HighNV-030

    The Manager loses all navigation in loading, error and offline states

    While the access check is unavailable, the Manager's tab bar and sidebar collapse to Home only, so a slow network leaves them no way to move. The Owner keeps all five tabs.

    Fix. Build the Manager's tabs from the last known operational context instead of dropping them when context.operational is unavailable (app-shell.tsx:183–185).

  11. 11HighNV-013

    Desktop Schedule has no visible or keyboard path to Add shift

    The band offers only "All locations" and "…", and the "…" menu has no Add shift or Build and publish. The grid's "+ Add" appears only on cell hover and is aria-hidden with tabIndex -1.

    Fix. Add a white "Add shift" pill in the band (it becomes "Publish N drafts" when drafts exist) and add Add shift and Build and publish to the "…" menu. Keep the hover "+ Add" as a shortcut.

  12. 12HighNV-027

    A time-off conflict looks like a normal shift

    The cell says she is off and also scheduled, with no warning colour. Things to do flags the same shift as "Fill Ana Colon's shift · Needs an Owner".

    Fix. When a cell has leave plus a shift, draw the block with an amber 2px inset ring, an amber WarningIcon, and the label "Needs cover". Make it link to the fill flow. Code: src/components/manager-weekly-roster.tsx:351–352.

  13. 13HighNV-029

    Approving a timecard ends on a blank page with no confirmation

    The summary, table and links disappear, leaving bare canvas. The tabs are dimmed and the panel shows only "Checking period timecards…" in 13px grey. There is no green "Approved" anywhere.

    Fix. Keep the table rendered (stale-while-revalidate). Flip the row's status to a green "Approved" chip immediately, and show a role="status" line in the panel: "Elena Ruiz's timecard is approved". Refresh in the background.

  14. 14HighNV-048

    The live clock is clipped at the band's edge, and AM/PM is lost

    At 1024 the band is clamp(320px, 36vw, 480px) = 368px, which leaves a 296px content box after 36px padding each side. The clock is clamp(5.5rem, 11.7vw, 8.25rem) = 120px. "10:43" alone measures about 306px in the shot, and the 30px day period plus the 10px gap add about 55px more.

    Fix. Size the clock to the band, not the viewport. Add container-type: inline-size to .band (clocker.module.css:56). Use .clock { font-size: clamp(4.5rem, 29cqi, 8.25rem); } (:72). At a 296px content box that is about 86px, so "10:43 p. m." fits. Alternatively, let .clock wrap the day period under the digits: flex-wrap: wrap on .clock, with .clock > span { flex-basis: 100% } only when it doesn't fit.

  15. 15HighNV-052

    The PIN lockout covers the whole tablet, but the screen reads as though it's about the next person

    The attempt budget is per device (pins.server.ts:62–70: "Reserve the shared/tablet attempt budget"; scope DEVICE). After someone else's wrong PINs, the next employee walks up to "Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes before trying again." The heading is still "Enter your PIN" (clocker-pin-gate.tsx:125).

    Fix. UI only; the server's limits stay as they are. When tone === 'wait', change the heading from "Enter your PIN" to "This tablet is paused". Add a second line: "Too many wrong PINs were entered on this tablet. Wait about five minutes, or ask a manager to record your time."

Decisions for Jose

These need a product call before anyone builds the fix. Each has the options and a recommendation.

HighNV-001Going offline wipes the loaded page while the banner says "Showing what was loaded"

When the phone or computer goes offline, should pages keep what was already loaded, or clear it?

  1. Keep the last loaded snapshot read-only, with an "Offline · updated 9:24 PM" line and actions disabled. Matches the banner and helps people on weak shop Wi-Fi.
  2. Keep clearing for privacy (the X-Nevora-Failure contract) and change the banner to "You're offline. Reconnect to see the latest."

Recommendation. Keep the snapshot for a person's own shift, hours and lists, and clear only when the app is paused because the person stepped away. Either way, the banner must stop promising something the page doesn't do.

HighNV-033The Time off list says "withdraw it", but the request page has no Withdraw

Can employees withdraw a waiting time-off request themselves?

  1. Yes: add a red-outline "Withdraw request" with a confirm on waiting requests.
  2. No: keep "contact your manager" and remove the promise from the list note.

Recommendation. Allow it for waiting requests. It saves the manager a step and the list already promises it.

HighNV-052The PIN lockout covers the whole tablet, but the screen reads as though it's about the next person

The Clocker PIN lockout is per tablet, so one person's wrong PINs block everyone. Keep that scope?

  1. Keep the device-wide lockout (current server rule) and change only the screen: "This tablet is paused" plus "ask a manager to record your time".
  2. Move to a per-person lockout so the next employee can still clock in.

Recommendation. Ship the screen change now; it needs no server work. Then decide on per-person scope with whoever owns PIN security.

MediumNV-124Payroll settings copy is audit language, and it is locked

Payroll copy is locked (DESIGN.MD:1320). Can it be rewritten in plain language?

  1. Unlock it for a supervised plain-language pass, with Jose approving each line.
  2. Keep it locked as-is until a legal or accounting review.

Recommendation. Unlock it for a supervised pass. Start with the four labels above, which change no legal meaning.

MediumNV-161The "On shift now" content is shown twice and takes the whole first screen

Lead Home repeats "On shift now" three ways. The extra sentence is in the Nov 8 Lead spec. Trim it?

  1. Drop the sentence when the hero already shows the shift, retitle the card "Your shift".
  2. Keep the Nov 8 spec as written.

Recommendation. Trim it. Things to do moves back onto the first phone screen.

MediumNV-186Sign-in headings end in periods, and the Spanish slogan is a different line

The mobile sign-in copy is frozen v1. May we drop the heading periods, and what is the Spanish slogan?

  1. Unfreeze for these two changes: no periods on headings, and a single approved Spanish slogan in brand.ts.
  2. Keep v1 as-is, and record "Tu día empieza aquí." as the approved Spanish slogan.

Recommendation. Drop the periods (matches voice.md and the page titles) and approve one Spanish slogan; a translation of "Brighter work ahead." keeps the brand line identical.

MediumNV-214The only action is Sign out, and the copy confuses Leads

The phone app blocks Leads and Managers with a Sign out page. Should Leads be allowed in the app?

  1. Allow Leads, who use the Employee screens on the web, into the app.
  2. Keep the block, but add "Open NEVORA in your browser" as the primary action and explain that shift leads use the browser.

Recommendation. Allow Leads, since their screens are the Employee screens. Until then, ship the browser button and clearer copy.

LowNV-274Sideways phones still show the old corporate layout

Sideways phones (844×390) still show the corporate page, as accepted in round 4. Revisit now?

  1. Give landscape phones the Direction B phone layout.
  2. Keep the accepted corporate layout for now.

Recommendation. Revisit after the High fixes; it is the last pre-B surface people can reach.

LowNV-289Repeated markers and repeated totals

When a Lead leads every shift, seven identical "Shift lead" chips appear. The chip is specified per block. Collapse it?

  1. One header line ("You lead all 7 shifts") and the chip only on today's block.
  2. Keep a chip on every block.

Recommendation. Collapse to one line when every shift is led.

LowNV-308Puerto Rico Spanish: "tiempo libre" means leisure, "Importe" is Spain usage

Which Spanish word should NEVORA use for paid time off?

  1. "Días libres" (solicitud de días libres): plain and common.
  2. "Licencia": more formal, closer to HR usage.

Recommendation. "Días libres" for the UI, matching the glossary; keep "licencia" for formal documents if needed.

LowNV-320Revoked: the destructive button sits between two neutral ones

Revoked alerts list Check again, Turn off alerts (red), Review app setup, with no primary. DESIGN lists this order. Reorder?

  1. Check again (teal), Review app setup (quiet), Turn off alerts (red outline) last.
  2. Keep DESIGN's order.

Recommendation. Reorder so the destructive action is last and one action is primary.

LowNV-323Small finder details

The Employee and Lead finder (Ctrl K) has no Actions. DESIGN marks this "default until Jose decides". Add them?

  1. Add Request time off, Swap a shift and Set availability as finder actions.
  2. Keep the finder to pages only for Employees and Leads.

Recommendation. Add the three actions; they are the most common employee tasks.

HighNV-005Accessibility

The live-figure tiles are invalid list markup (axe "serious")

Owner phone · Owner desktop · Manager · Employee · Lead · Tablet

Every Home live strip renders <dl><div><a><dt/><dd/></a></div></dl>. A link between the group and the term breaks the list, so screen readers lose the label and value pairing. axe flags it on 60 audits (368 nodes), for every role and at tablet width.

Fix. Render the tiles as <ul class="b-live"><li><a aria-label=…><span>label</span><span>value</span></a></li></ul>. The link's aria-label already carries "Late: 0. Missed clock-ins".

No findings match. Clear the search or pick another area.

Patterns across the app

  1. Status colour has no single source. Red, amber, green and teal are chosen per screen, so the same state changes colour (open shifts, Published, over target, Needs an Owner, the bell). One status-to-tone table in the kit fixes most of them.
  2. Every state is built differently. Loading, error, empty and offline appear in about seven shapes, none with an icon or colour, and offline throws away what was loaded. One state card and one offline rule cover all roles.
  3. Counts and formats are computed per screen. Timecard counts, paydays, hours and time ranges each come from a different calculation or formatter. One selector for payroll counts and one formatter for hours and ranges remove a whole class of disagreement.
  4. Tablets got the desktop layout without a touch pass. From 768px the desktop CSS applies to touch screens: 28–40px targets, hover tints that stick, keyboard hints, labels only on hover, and phone layouts stretched to 726px.
  5. Wayfinding is phone-shaped. Back links and the lit tab name different parents, and desktop lacks entry points the phone has (Help, Add shift, Team filters, Attention).
  6. The band has unclear rules. White text on the band uses 17 alphas, the band is painted seven ways, and some pages clip labels or titles under it. Two text tokens and one band recipe settle it.
  7. Older layers leak through. Loading skeletons, the phone 404, the Manager's error card and some greys still come from the Quiet and corp eras. The !important ladder makes each fix risky; cascade layers are the structural fix.
  8. Wording drifts into audit language. Recovery steps say "protected snapshot", "source revision" and "reconcile"; one concept has up to five names; Spanish mixes "Owner" and "dueño". The glossary below sets one term per concept.
  9. Phone and desktop show different content. The same page shows different figures, actions or order by width (Attention 4, Team filters, Time's live state, Insights export).
  10. The Clocker band doesn't follow the card. The band stays green "Tablet registered" during offline, reconnect and lockout errors, and blocked states fall back to one generic "Check Connection" button.

Wording: one term per concept

From the copy audit. Use the English and Puerto Rico Spanish terms; retire the rest. Rename together with the QA scripts that press these labels.

Already good

  • One icon library: Phosphor only, in 187 files, with no lucide, heroicons or emoji.
  • No horizontal overflow at any width: overflowX was 0 in all 867 audits, including 320px. Every audited page has an h1.
  • Reduced-motion guards on every moving keyframe animation, and no transition: all anywhere.
  • Every icon-only button and link has an accessible name.
  • Focus rings are consistent: 2px white on the band and 2px teal on cards.
  • The Ctrl K finder is a native modal dialog: focus is trapped, Escape closes it and focus returns to the opener.
  • Rail tooltips appear on hover and on keyboard focus, can be dismissed with Escape, and can be hovered (WCAG 1.4.13).
  • Sheets are native modal dialogs with drag-to-dismiss, Escape, outside tap, and no travel under reduced motion.
  • Form validation sets aria-invalid and aria-describedby and moves focus to the first invalid field.
  • Sign-in: labelled inputs, correct autocomplete tokens, 16px phone inputs (no iOS zoom), role="alert" errors, and a busy Sign in that refuses a second press.
  • Long names wrap rather than truncate on the Manager screens checked.
  • The Manager's time-off request detail is a model: a clear amber staffing warning, the consequence written out, teal Approve and grey Decline.
  • Clocker ergonomics are strong: 76–96px keys, 84px action rows, optically centred rings, and four digits plus Continue plus one action to punch.
  • Native Alerts follows the approved ring language, keeps the reassurance line in every state, and moves focus to the confirm and back.
  • Safe areas are handled in code: viewport-fit=cover, and the band, back link and tab bar pad with env(safe-area-inset-*).
  • Status chips in Requests and Pay use amber, green and grey correctly, and Pay's ink hero passes contrast.
  • Spanish copy uses tú consistently, with complete ¿…? punctuation.

What this review could not check

  • Screen-reader output (VoiceOver, NVDA) was not run anywhere.
  • Real devices: touch behaviour, press feel, hover latching and real safe-area insets. The phone-app captures used browser emulation, so insets were 0.
  • Phone keyboard order: the 390 Tab walks were captured while pages were still loading, so focus order in phone content is unconfirmed (see the Tab finding).
  • Reduced motion was checked only for the shift sheet, card entrance and Clocker; not for sign-in, Lead, Owner desktop or tablets.
  • 200% zoom was not run. 320px reflow holds.
  • Menus and popovers on Owner and Manager phones were not opened; phone More and account sheets and the Manager inbox sheet were not captured. A few captures mis-clicked (inbox sheet-open landed on the Schedule skeleton).
  • Tablets: menus, side panels, the finder, the expanded rail, keyboard order, loading/error/offline, long names and validation were not captured at tablet width.
  • Landscape phones: the 844×390 captures were dropped by the collector except five Employee shots.
  • Native select option lists and date pickers, which headless Chromium doesn't draw.
  • Exact colour pairs behind the 4.26–4.30:1 grey lines: the probe may have sampled the wrong background. Re-measure in a browser before acting.
  • Cascade winners where layers compete, forced-colours mode, and the rendered effect of a stored dark-theme preference.
  • Whether switch rows act as labels, and whether ::after hit extensions survive at tablet width.
  • Why Notifications failed on its default route, and whether the five timecard counts are different scopes or a bug.
  • Escape and focus return on the timecard panel; whether the finder reaches Help.
  • Sign-in states not captured: too many attempts, signing in, activated, account being deleted, passkey and Face ID, request received, password updated, a valid activation, expired or used links (the "bad" captures showed the default state), Mobile Access off on phones, and the public error page.
  • Clocker states not captured: Checking your clock, Previous action needs review (another person), tablet without PINs, PIN verified with punches off, and the camera live, review, error and unknown states; Spanish at 768 and 390. Clocker and component captures have no automated audit data.
  • Phone app: Owner and Lead shells at desktop widths, the Notifications Settings entry (feature flag off), the blur-pause and the settings deep link.
  • Validation on Add employee and New location at 390, Availability and Can't-work validation, and the shift pickup failure state.
  • Copy: Spanish overflow at 320, server strings beyond the Clocker and recovery, company data (names, break types, positions), legal page bodies, locked payroll sentences and the owner-advisor output.
  • The Clocker's real wait across its three sequential requests was not measured.

Screenshots used fictional local data captured Mon, Nov 9, 2026 around 8–10 PM Puerto Rico time, at commit e561e97c. Severity: High blocks or confuses a task or fails accessibility; Medium is a visible inconsistency or friction; Low is polish.
